chapter: California, Cats and the Fiddle, the Tatum trio
title: Second record date, bassist change, and getting along in the group
summary: On a later session George Steinbeck replaced Chuck Barksdale; Grimes arranged Blue Skies and wrote Lawdy Claudy and Stomp, Stomp.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: 2nd record date w/ C & F. George Steinbeck replaced Chuck Barksdale on bass, ...
Oh yeah, George, yeah. Very good bass player. Think Chuck got sick, I believe. Went back to Chicago. Anyhow George, he was a good solid bass player -- he was with Basil for a while I think.
Tunes you did at that session --
I arranged Blue Skies; Stomp, Stomp I made up --
Get along well with other guys in C & F.

Yeah, sure, we got along good. Had to 'cause we had to rehearse daily. It was no let up. Because they had such a repertoire and I had to learn all these things and the parts that go with 'em, not just sing in the lead -- harmony. I was enthused. I enthused them. I had new stuff. The piano helped, and everything helped, and we had a little dance goin'.
Did you dance with them too?
Yeah. I was an asset. I was an asset to the group.
Another song you recorded with them was Lawdy Claudy.
Oh yeah. Another thing I made up. I don't know if I played piano on that, I know it was a saying at that time a hot saying, you know, like slang, as you might say, so I made a song out of it.
